# Scheme Management {#sec-tech-schemes}

The scheme is the reference data every later step is measured against, so how it
is fetched and — more importantly — how a database *records which scheme it
belongs to* is load-bearing for typing, for the compatibility gate and for
classical-MLST resolution. This chapter documents the modules behind the Scheme
Browser and the cgMLST Overview panel.

## The scheme browser module {#sec-tech-schemes-browser}

`app/view/scheme_browser.R` drives the species picker, the scheme details card,
the download target, and the hand-off to `main.R` that loads the database it just
created. Note the boundary: this module can only load the database it has *just
downloaded* (`Scheme_Browser$last_download`); opening an arbitrary existing file
is `app/view/landing_page.R`'s job.

```{.r filename="app/view/scheme_browser.R"}
# Remember the path of the last successful download so the
# "Load Database" click hands over this database rather than the
# current (possibly changed) input selection.
Scheme_Browser$last_download <- db_location
```

Its supporting logic is split across three modules:

- `app/logic/scheme_browser.R` — species metadata, scheme-identity resolution,
  target-path assembly, and download orchestration.
- `app/logic/schemes.R` — the catalogue of supported schemes.
- `app/logic/pymlst.R` — the actual download, shelled out to pyMLST
  (@sec-tech-typing).

Species metadata (taxonomy, descriptions and per-species artwork) is loaded once
and cached (`species_metadata()`, `get_species_details()`, `get_species_img()`),
so the browser can present a rich picker without re-fetching on every render.

## Downloading a scheme {#sec-tech-schemes-download}

Creating a new database downloads the scheme and records its provenance. The
download itself runs through pyMLST's `wgMLST` importer:

```{.r filename="app/logic/pymlst.R"}
#' Download cgMLST Scheme via wgMLST
download_cgmlst_scheme <- function(db_path, scheme, overwrite = ...) { ... }
```

Alongside the alleles, the scheme's published summary and its target loci are
stored in the database so later reads never need the network again:

- `download_scheme_overview()` writes the `scheme_overview` table (locus count,
  seed genome, the published cluster-distance threshold).
- `download_scheme_targets()` writes the target locus list.
- `get_scheme_overview()` fetches the HTML summary from the repository.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-scheme-download
%%| fig-cap: "Creating a database: pick a species, resolve the scheme, download alleles + metadata into a fresh .db."
flowchart LR
  S["Species picker<br/>(scheme_browser)"] --> R["resolve_scheme_key()"]
  R --> D["pyMLST wgMLST<br/>(download_cgmlst_scheme)"]
  D --> O["download_scheme_overview()<br/>download_scheme_targets()"]
  O --> DB[("new .db<br/>mlst · sequences · hashes ·<br/>scheme_overview")]
```

## Recording which scheme a database was built from {#sec-tech-schemes-identity}

A database must be able to say, unambiguously, which scheme it belongs to — the
compatibility gate (@sec-tech-interop) and the classical-MLST resolver
(@sec-tech-typing) both depend on it. `resolve_scheme_key()` establishes that
identity:

```{.r filename="app/logic/scheme_browser.R"}
#' Resolve the Scheme a Database Was Built From
resolve_scheme_key <- function(species = NULL, scheme_overview = NULL) { ... }
```

::: {.callout-important title="Scheme identity: overview URL first, species only as fallback"}
The resolver prefers the `scheme_overview` URL/abbreviation — a precise
per-scheme identifier — and uses the species name from `mlst_type` only as a
fallback. The reason is that the stored species name is not always trustworthy:
pyMLST's parsing can letter-mangle it (the "*Klebsiella neumoniae*" class of
bug), which is exactly why `migrate_species_name()` repairs it on load
(@sec-db-migrations) and why species is never used as an *exact* taxon key on its
own.
:::

## The cgMLST Overview panel {#sec-tech-schemes-inspect}

`app/view/database_cgmlst.R` is one of the five Database sub-app panels
(@sec-arch-subapp). It exposes two read-only views of the loaded scheme:

- **Scheme Info** — the `scheme_overview` values: organism, locus count, seed
  genome, cluster threshold.
- **Loci Info** — one row per target locus, with the number of distinct alleles
  seen for it in this database, drilling down to individual alleles and their
  sequences:

```{.r filename="app/logic/database_functions.R"}
#' Returns scheme targets supplemented with distinct allele counts per target locus.
load_loci_info    <- function(db_path) { ... }
#' Retrieves distinct allele IDs for a locus and counts isolate occurrences.
load_locus_alleles <- function(db_path, gene) { ... }
#' Exports all sequence entries assigned to a specified locus as FASTA strings.
locus_fasta       <- function(db_path, gene) { ... }
```

## Chapter summary

- `scheme_browser.R` (view) + `scheme_browser.R`/`schemes.R`/`pymlst.R` (logic)
  handle species metadata, scheme resolution and download; the view can load only
  the database it just created.
- Downloading runs through pyMLST's `wgMLST` importer, and the scheme's overview
  and target loci are cached into the `.db`.
- `resolve_scheme_key()` prefers the overview URL over the stored species name,
  which pyMLST can mangle.
- `database_cgmlst.R` reads the scheme back through `load_loci_info()`,
  `load_locus_alleles()` and `locus_fasta()`.
